To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the state sums in two dimensions introduced in 2001 by Fukuma, Kawai and Hosono are generalized to a class of models that are sensitive to spin structures on surfaces; (b) an algebraic criterion is given for the models in this class to distinguish between topologically-inequlivalent spin structures; (c) examples of models that distinguish spin structures are given.
we constructed a new family of 2D topological field theories and showed that they are sensitive to spin structure, which was previously unknown.
we have generalized the state sum models introduced by Fukuma et al. to non-symmetric Frobe-nius algebras.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the state sum models of 2D quantum gravity.
the study of two-dimensional quantum field theories.
the construction and analysis of two-dimensional state sum models, with the aim of understanding the role that algebraic data play in determining the partition function of the state sum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the state sum models are not a good tool for distinguishing spin structures.
the state sum model is a very useful tool for studying topological invariants of surfaces.
the models introduced in this thesis do not provide an effective way of calculating spin structures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spin structure is a topological structure that can be detected by a state sum model if the algebraic data is suitably augmented.
we generalise a state sum model to a model that can be used for computing the partition function on any oriented surface with spin structure.
we have found a new way to distinguish topologically- inequivalent spin structures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the partition function of the model can be used to compute the signature of the spin structure on any closed surface, and the model can be defined on a large class of surfaces with boundary.
the spin-structure dependence of state sum models is a natural consequence of the algebraic structure of the data.
the spin structure of a surface is encoded by a Frobenius algebra, and this algebraic data can be used to construct a state sum model.
